question.text: Let the equation of the plane <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi></math> containing the line <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo>-</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mi>z</mi></math> be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>a</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>)</mo></math> and the distance of the plane <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi></math> from the point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>27</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>)</mo></math> be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>c</mi></math>. solution.text:
Given,

The line  x+101=y-8-2=z1 which passes through the point (-10,8,0)

Also given the equation of plane  ax+by+3z=2(a+b) and the point (-10,8,0) will lie on it as plane contains the line,

So, a-10+b×8+3×0=2(a+b)

⇒b=2a ......1

Now product of direction ratio of line and direction ratio of plane will be zero as they both are perpendicular,

So, a×1+b×-2+3×1=0

⇒a-2b+3=0 ........2

Now on solving equation 1 & 2 we get, a=1and b=2

Hence, the equation of plane will be,

x+2y+3z-6=0

Now distance from (1,27,7) from plane x+2y+3z-6=0 will be,

c=1+54+21-614=7014=514
